items.text: Inherited Wings
Floridian Branch of Space Center, 1969

items.speaker: Space Center Employee
items.text: On behalf of the Space Center, we really wanted to thank you for your service these past years, Madam Lucy.

items.speaker: Space Center Employee
items.text: I brought you a few brochures for you to look over with some great vacation spots. Sunny beaches, high-class resorts—you'll have lots of things to do.
She accepts the offered papers gracefully, but there is no real joy in it for her. A holiday resort is no different to her from a quiet office with an adequate power supply.

items.speaker: Space Center Employee
items.text: Oh, and I included the schedule for the moon landing broadcast. Didn't want you to miss it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Would you ring the Bay Shore High School for me? I need to talk to Ms. Joanna.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am sure she will be in her office now.

items.speaker: Space Center Employee
items.text: O-okay.
Hello.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hello, Ms. Joanna. I am letting you know I will arrive later today, before ...
She looks up at the clock.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Shortly before dusk. Yes, see you later.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Okay. I'll wait for you here.
Lucy hangs up without another word. Never one for formalities.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I will need a ride to Bay Shore.

items.speaker: Space Center Employee
items.text: Sure. I'll arrange for a car to pick you up outside the center.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: How long will it take to get there?

items.speaker: Space Center Employee
items.text: Less than an hour, if the traffic isn't too bad.

items.speaker: Space Center Employee
items.text: And that shouldn't be a worry. The military has arranged a cordon all around the center.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Good. I am glad to see that the Space Center remains as efficient as ever.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You have prepared for everything with more than adequate redundancies. I am looking forward to witnessing this historic moment.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I will also need my luggage and equipment brought to the car before I leave. If that will not be too much trouble.
Bay Shore Middle School, 1969
Adolescents, even of the older variety, have always confused Lucy. The patterns of their behavior unpredictable and frequently irrational.
As she arrives, she is instantly reminded of that discomfort. The students begin flocking to her.

items.speaker: Student I
items.text: Woah, a robot! Hey Jack, Annie, come check it out! A real-live robot!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Please allow me through.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Please.
The mechanical woman is surrounded by students, forming an impenetrable wall of questions.
Give her some space.
Is that how any of you would treat a guest?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Oh, Joanna. You look healthy. Have you improved your diet and exercise regime?

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Is that robot for: "good to see you?" Well, I'm glad you haven't changed too much from hanging around with all those brainiacs without me.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: A healthy body and a clear mind will improve performance in humans. And even I need regular maintenance.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Without it, I might experience unnecessary component failures—Or, sorry, I mean to say, it is good to see you, too.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Alright then, as for all of you, I'm sure you are eager to hit the beach. Grab your things and get going.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: I need a moment to speak to our guest. Off you go.
Joanna's Office, 1969

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: These are their trophies. I know it's not as glamorous as working for the Space Center, but teaching has rewards of its own.
The trophies are not inconsiderable, and by the reaction of her students, she has most certainly achieved her own kind of success.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am glad to see that you have found something meaningful to do after you left.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: And I'm happy to see you finally taking a break.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: I was beginning to think you'd be working until your wiring melted.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hmm? As long as my power supply is stable, there should be no risk of damage to my wiring.
As if matching her statement, the lights begin to flicker in the building.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Probably just the generator. Don't worry your pretty metal head over it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Oh no! You should—

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Relax, Lucy. We've all gotten used to it.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: That Space Center of yours is a bit of a power suck. But a few flickering bulbs aren't a bad price to pay for the moon.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: It shouldn't affect the broadcast. But we'll just have to hope the system can hold up until then.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: But, that's why we always have a plan B, right?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Agreed. People underestimate their value. But in an emergency, redundancies always prove their worth.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But best not to leave it to chance.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Found it.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Remember this?
They unfold a tattered old draft. A gift for Joanna to celebrate her retirement. One of the few human rituals she has come to value.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am happy that our modern advances in aviation have, at last, made this project viable.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But, with my other work, I have not had any time to work on it. I am glad you have been able to make use of it.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Ah, well I had the time you didn't, but you're the one that's really driven this project forward.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Attending your experiments and record-keeping are far from significant contributions.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And it has been a long time since I have done even that.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What is your current progress?

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Not as far as your rocket, for certain. But we're making real progress.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Invention takes time. I cannot fault you for lacking the same resources I have access to at the Space Center.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It is remarkable just how much progress we have made even in the last decade.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And it has been an international effort, even despite our differences. It is remarkable how much we have learned from the Soviet Space Program.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: The competition starts as soon as someone takes the lead.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: The Baikonur Cosmodrome sent the first satellite above the stratosphere, and we sent the second one.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Then they launched a manned rocket into space. We had to catch up with them, so we made our own.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Now they're aiming at the moon, Mars, and maybe the galaxy is next.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: But we're not going to be left watching their exhaust this time. Now we're going to take the lead.
A prideful smile stretches over her face.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I appreciate your competitiveness.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It makes us work faster, think smarter, run farther.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Once we leave those first footsteps there, in the dust of another world,

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: there is no telling how far humanity will run.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There will be new footprints, new detectors, new astronauts, new bases, and then settlers. The Space Center has made plans for all of it.
Her friend has turned back to the trophy case.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Jack and Peter are always competing with each other. They've pushed themselves so hard, and each time they fly a little higher and a little longer than the last time.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: I think near half of these are Jack's, and most of the rest are Peter's. I doubt they'd have gotten this far if the other wasn't there to push them another step.
Their awards tell the story as well as she could, small incremental gains, iteration over iteration. But each victory was a badge of honor.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: So, you have them working on the project too?

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: I brought them on board as soon as they showed interest. Their work is largely based on your designs.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: That prototype you sent us served as an excellent model.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Is that so? It had been shelved for a long time.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Every once in a while, I would take it out again, whenever I found a new technology or material that could be incorporated into the design.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It has been the work of decades, centuries almost. I am very glad to hear you have made progress on it.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Only because you never gave up on it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: A project should not be idly abandoned, not until all avenues of success have been exhausted.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And that is a rare case.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: In fact, perhaps I am optimistic, but I think that such a case almost never happens.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The only real challenge is in what projects deserve our time and resources. There is no way to juggle everything. Sometimes other work must take precedent.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: That's why we share these ideas. What was it you always said? "Like an ember passed from hand to hand?"

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: C'mon, Lucy. Let me show you what we've done with that ember.
It was an uplifting invitation.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: After two years, we're finally seeing the sparks take flame. Though it isn't much now. Just something for them to play around with.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You mean, you have actually made something of my designs?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: How did you overcome the issues with fuel capacity?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Were you able to find a rigid material capable of withstanding the drag force? One that is still flexible enough to allow the pilot to pivot in the air?
How long had she kept that ember? How many before them had thrown it away? But now, it seems that it is burning once more.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Ha-ha-ha-ha!

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Oh, Lucy, I'm sure you have a million questions. But let's just go see our pilots in action.
